I had a recent roadtrip and downloaded the audio book for A Game of Thrones. I guess the main thing that really sticks out now is how rich the world is from the get-go. People and events are set up in the first few chapters, and sometimes you don't see them until the other books.

Mance Rayder is mentioned in the first main chapter of the series, Bran I, but I believe doesn't make his actual appearance until A Storm of Swords. Ned mentions the Blackfish as being Knight of the Gate in the Vale in an early chapter, and we don't see him until much later.

It's kind of nice, if you pay attention, you'll know stuff about places before the characters even reach there.

That although I realized Jon was 'fragged' in his last chapter in ADWD, I have never attributed any significance to the numerology of the books/chapters. In other words, I did not realize that Jon Snow dies in Jon chapter XIII of the fifth book...in other words, Jon 5:13. If GRRM uses the King James Bible as a literary inspiration, John 5:13 states:

"These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God."

Even though I realize that a literal translation of the text refers to the reader, not the subject; the language still seems eerily on-topic.

I missed a LOT of details about the ADWD Winterfell plotline on the first read through. I've said it before, but I really do think that's the most densely packed portion of the entire series so far in terms of minor details that are likely to be consequential.

The story about the Stark kids playing in the Winterfell crypts. As children, Robb lured Sansa, Arya, and Bran into the crypts, and Jon jumped out of a tomb covered in white flour (like a ghost) to scare them. Might not mean anything, but with what happens to Jon at the end of ADWD it definitely seemed more significant on re-read.

There seems to be A LOT of stuff like that in GoT. Moreso than any the other books. Probably because GRRM still thought the series would be shorter at that point.

GoT - Arya

Robb took them all the way down to the end, past Grandfather and Brandon and Lyanna, to show them their own tombs. Sansa kept looking at the stubby little candle, anxious that it might go out. Old Nan had told her there were spiders down here, and rats as big as dogs. Robb smiled when she said that. "There are worse things than spiders and rats," he whispered. "This is where the dead walk." That was when they heard the sound, low and deep and shivery. Baby Bran had clutched at Arya's hand.

When the spirit stepped out of the open tomb, pale white and moaning for blood, Sansa ran shrieking for the stairs, and Bran wrapped himself around Robb's leg,sobbing. Arya stood her ground and gave the spirit a punch. It was only Jon, covered with flour. "You stupid," she told him, "you scared the baby," but Jon and Robb just laughed and laughed, and pretty soon Bran and Arya were laughing too.
